The holocaust obviously happened, I'm not a retard.

However, holocaust denial is illegal according to Swiss law, which Voat follows. The law says:

Whoever publicly, by word, writing, image, gesture, acts of violence or any other manner, demeans or discriminates against an individual or a group of individuals because of their race, their ethnicity or their religion in a way which undermines human dignity, or on those bases, denies, coarsely minimizes or seeks to justify a genocide or other crimes against humanity [...] shall be punished with up to three years' imprisonment or a fine.

This overly broad language seems to ban a lot of stuff like shitniggerssay too, or maybe even /r/atheism! It basically bans offensive content as long as the offense "demeans someone because of their race, their ethnicity or their religion in a way which undermines human dignity", whatever the hell that means.

I'm not a fan of either conspiritards or haters, but at least being one is legal under US laws. Reddit didn't start banning subreddits because they legally had to, they did it because they (for whatever reason) wanted to. However,

I just don't understand why following the Swiss freedom of speech laws is supposed to be positive for Voat, since they're way more restrictive than the US freedom of speech laws. Can anyone explain? Are people just blinded by Switzerlands legendary (and recently increasingly inaccurate) status as a privacy haven or is there actually something I'm missing?
The holocaust did not happen. Did I just break Swiss law/Voat rules?

Are people just blinded by Switzerlands legendary (and recently increasingly inaccurate) status as a privacy haven or is there actually something I'm missing?

Nah, I think you're not too far off. I'm Swiss and I don't mind the restrictive freedom of speech laws that much. They're liberally enforced and nothing I want to express falls into a legal gray zone anyway. Not that this is a good argument, I know, but when you look at the public political discourse here in Switzerland you can for instance still be xenophobic and discuss immigration without fearing prison time. I can't think of an instance where this restriction lead to actual restrictions on public discourse, so I don't care that much.

Where it came to play recently was when a political party insinuated that a whole part of the population was potentially violently criminal. They got a fine for launching a nationwide campaign... So yeah, you gotta be stupid to actually get prison time. On the other hand that alone isn't a good argument either to be for restrictive freedom of speech laws.

All I'm trying to do here is to put these restrictions into perspective. This is not North Korea, Russia or even Germany by far.

Either way: I agree, you can't really call Voat a free speech forum if it has to follow the Swiss laws. Even when most of us would not have to worry.
Didn't break the rules or the law as far as I know, but you've done a great job of wasting my time.
